correctness.rationale: The covariance and grounded inverse formulas are correct. The transfer-current kernel for the uniform spanning tree of \(K_n\) is \(K=n^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}B\), so determinantal two-edge marginals give variance \(2(n-2)/n^2\), covariance \(-1/n^2\) for incident distinct edges, and zero covariance for disjoint edges. This is exactly \(n^{-2}L_{L(K_n)}\). The unsigned-incidence identities reduce the line-graph Laplacian to two nonzero eigenspaces, and the displayed pseudoinverse followed by the standard grounding identity gives all six precision orbits. Substitution into the precision normalization gives the six partial-correlation formulas. The actual package checker enumerates Prüfer trees through \(n=7\) and verifies every grounded product exactly through \(n=12\). Independently, I rebuilt the rational grounded covariance and inverted it exactly at \(n=6,7\), obtaining the stated diagonal classes and entrywise positivity. The finite checks are supplementary; the universal proof is the transfer-current and exact incidence-matrix calculation.
residual_risks: The partial correlations are linear least-squares partial correlations, not nonlinear conditional correlations.
The result is specific to the complete host graph after one coordinate is grounded.

originality.rationale: The novelty-bearing formulas are a routine same-object specialization of stronger published machinery. Burton and Pemantle's transfer-impedance theorem gives every finite-dimensional marginal of a uniform spanning tree from the transfer-current matrix. On \(K_n\), inserting \(L_{K_n}^{+}=n^{-1}(I-n^{-1}J)\) makes the kernel \(n^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}B\), so the entire covariance matrix follows immediately from whether two edges meet. After that identification, the remaining claim is an elementary inversion of a grounded Laplacian of the classical line graph \(L(K_n)=J(n,2)\): the unsigned incidence identities printed in the audited proof already diagonalize the matrix, and the standard grounded-pseudoinverse identity gives the precision entries. Thus the exact orbit values and their normalized partial correlations are mechanically implied by a published same-object determinantal theorem plus standard Laplacian linear algebra, even though I did not locate these six numbers printed verbatim.
residual_risks: A statistics source might print the precision formulas explicitly, but explicit prior printing is unnecessary for this implication-based rejection.

The result introduces no new dependence theorem, boundary phenomenon, or difficult exact invariant beyond what the prior determinantal law and standard Laplacian algebra already encode. Under the common value bar, convenience of an explicit table is not enough to make this routine specialization independently valuable.
